message.content:
Add a polished, animated **logo carousel / marquee** to the Nxeon marketing landing page (/opt/nxeon, Next.js 15 + Tailwind) to build trust early — an "integrates with / works with / powered by" strip of technology logos.

## HONESTY REQUIREMENT (non-negotiable)
Frame it as **technologies Nxeon integrates with / runs**, NOT as customers, clients, partners, or endorsements. Use headings like "Works with your stack", "Integrates with the tools you already use", or "Powered by". Do **NOT** write copy implying these companies are customers, partners, investors, or endorse Nxeon. Only include a logo if the integration genuinely exists in this codebase — verify each one before including it.

## Verify what's real first (do NOT run git or `npm run build`)
Confirm actual integrations by inspecting the code, then include only those. Strong candidates to verify:
- **Cloudflare** — `lib/cloudflare-dns.ts` + a brand-new OAuth integration (`lib/cloudflare-oauth.ts`, `app/api/integrations/cloudflare/*`) — genuinely integrated.
- **Stripe** — `lib/stripe.ts` (payments) ✓
- **Proxmox** — `lib/proxmox.ts` (the whole hypervisor layer) ✓
- **Docker** — control panel + migration bring-up ✓
- **Anthropic / Claude** — Claude Code pre-installed + AI builder (`lib/ai-build.ts`); there's an existing `components/marketing/ClaudeMark.tsx` — reuse it ✓
- **Let's Encrypt / certbot** — SSL issuance (`worker/ssl.ts`) ✓
- **WordPress, Ghost, Nextcloud** — one-click apps (`worker/apps.ts`) ✓
- **Ubuntu, Debian, AlmaLinux, Rocky, Fedora, Alpine, Arch, CentOS** — OS templates ✓
- **MySQL/MariaDB, PostgreSQL** — control-panel databases ✓
- **nginx / Apache** — websites bundle ✓
- **Minecraft / game servers** — game plans ✓
- **Name.com** — the domain registrar (`lib/registrar.ts`) — verify before using its mark
- Others already present as assets: cPanel, Plesk, Portainer, Grafana, Gitea, Jellyfin, Node.js, Redis, WireGuard, OpenVPN, Pi-hole, Vaultwarden, Uptime Kuma, Caddy, Steam.
Drop anything you can't substantiate.

## Assets
- **Reuse `public/logos/*.svg`** — ~30 real logo SVGs already exist (ubuntu, debian, docker, wordpress, nextcloud, ghost, nodejs, cpanel, plesk, grafana, minecraft, etc.). Check the directory listing and use what's there via the existing `AppLogo` component if it fits.
- For brands with **no local asset** (e.g. Cloudflare, Stripe, Proxmox, Let's Encrypt, PostgreSQL, MySQL, nginx): do **NOT** download third-party logo files into the repo. Instead render a clean, consistently-styled **text wordmark** (the brand name set in the design system's type, in the monochrome treatment described below). A tasteful uniform wordmark strip looks deliberate and sidesteps any licensing/trademark-asset issue.

## The component
Create `components/marketing/LogoMarquee.tsx` (or similar) and mount it on the landing page (`app/page.tsx`) high up — just under the hero / above or near the first content section — so it does its trust job early. Match the existing marketing system (study `components/marketing/*`: `Section`, `SectionTitle`, `Reveal`, the dark navy/violet tokens, existing keyframes/animation utilities).

Requirements:
- **Infinite seamless marquee**: duplicate the logo list and translate the track by exactly -50% with a CSS keyframe animation for a gapless loop (no JS ticker, no new deps). Two rows scrolling in opposite directions looks great if it suits the design — your call.
- **Monochrome → color on hover** (e.g. `grayscale opacity-60` → full color/opacity), smooth transition, so it reads as a calm trust strip rather than a rainbow.
- **Edge fade masks** (CSS mask-image / gradient overlays) so logos fade in/out at the container edges instead of hard-cutting.
- **Pause on hover** (`animation-play-state: paused`).
- **`prefers-reduced-motion`**: no animation — render a static, centered, wrapped grid of the same logos.
- Responsive (smaller logos/faster loop on mobile), accessible: proper `alt`/`aria-label` per logo, `aria-hidden` on the duplicated track so screen readers don't read the list twice, and the section labelled sensibly.
- Keep it performant: CSS transform animation only, `will-change: transform`.

## Constraints
- No new npm deps. Do NOT touch: `lib/cloudflare-*`, `app/api/integrations/*`, `lib/actions-websites.ts`, `lib/actions-migrate.ts`, `components/customer/*`, `lib/registrar.ts`, `lib/actions-domains*`, `lib/domain-transfer.ts`, `prisma/schema.prisma`, `worker/*` — other agents own those. You own `components/marketing/*` (new file) and `app/page.tsx`.
- Do NOT run git or `npm run build`. Write/Edit may time out on a hook — fall back to Bash heredocs and verify.
- Verify ONLY with `cd /opt/nxeon && npx tsc --noEmit 2>&1 | grep -v "test/.*test.ts"` (clean for your files).

Report: the final logo list and the evidence for each integration, which used real SVG assets vs. text wordmarks, the exact heading/copy used (and confirm it makes no partnership/customer claim), the animation technique, and the reduced-motion fallback.

Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.

content.thinking:
I've verified the dependencies are in place, so now I'm building the LogoMarquee component as a server component. I'm defining a data structure where each logo entry has a name, optional family field pointing to SVG files in the public directory, and a hint, with special handling for the Claude logo.

The layout uses a two-row marquee scrolling in opposite directions, with each item containing a logo chip and label. I'm working through the styling approach — considering whether to use white chips at reduced opacity or apply a brightness-invert filter to render logos as white silhouettes in the resting state, then restore full color on hover. The challenge is handling logos like Ghost that are already very dark and would disappear against the navy background when colored.

I'm settling on applying the invert-brightness filter to make logos white silhouettes at reduced opacity, then on hover removing the filter to show true colors while simultaneously revealing a semi-transparent white background chip behind the logo. This gives dark logos a backdrop when they're in color, creating a clean reveal effect. The marquee pauses on hover, so individual items can be highlighted without disrupting the animation.

For text-only wordmarks like Cloudflare and Stripe, I'm keeping them as simple text that transitions from slate-gray to white on hover. The ClaudeMark SVG gets the same filter treatment as image logos. I'm also deciding to pair SVG marks with their name text to keep the layout consistent across all items — mark plus name side by side — which improves legibility and uniformity.

Now I'm working through the seamless loop math for the marquee track... The cleanest approach is to apply the gap as a margin on each item rather than using the container's gap property. This way, each item takes up width plus gap, making the track exactly twice the width of one list, so a -50% translate lands perfectly at the seam. I'll use `margin-inline-end` for uniform spacing across all items.

For animation timing, I'll use a CSS variable per row and add a media query to speed things up on mobile. When reduced motion is preferred, I need to hide the duplicate track and switch the layout to a wrapped flex grid centered on the page, removing the animation and mask entirely. The tricky part is structuring the markup so I can selectively hide just the duplicate without breaking the gap calculations.

If each item carries its own margin-right instead of relying on a gap property, the math works out perfectly: the track width becomes exactly twice the single-row width, and the -50% offset creates a seamless loop. For the reduced motion state, I'll hide the duplicate list and apply flex-wrap with center justification to both the track and individual lists, collapsing everything into a centered grid layout.

I'm also adding `will-change: transform` to optimize the animation performance, applying a horizontal linear-gradient mask for the edge fade effect (with webkit prefix for compatibility), and using `animation-direction: reverse` on the second row to make it scroll the opposite way. For accessibility, I'll wrap the marquee in a region with an aria-label since it's already inside a Section primitive.

For the logo images, I'm using empty alt text since the adjacent text label already identifies each brand, and marking the images as `aria-hidden` to prevent screen readers from duplicating the name — though the spec wants alt per logo, repeating "Docker Docker" would be worse, so this is the right compromise. I'll stick with `alt=""` and `aria-hidden` on the images to keep the accessible name clean—just the visible text label. For mobile, I'm scaling down the logo sizes and shortening animation durations. Now I'm organizing the integrations into two rows, starting with the platform and infrastructure tier: Cloudflare, Stripe, Proxmox, Docker, and Claude.

Continuing with the rest of the first row—Let's Encrypt, nginx, Apache, PostgreSQL, and then deciding between MySQL and MariaDB. Both are genuinely used in the app, so I'm leaning toward including them as separate entries rather than combining them into one awkward label.

Now moving into the second row for "what you can run"—WordPress, Ghost, Nextcloud, cPanel, Plesk, Grafana, Portainer, Gitea, Jellyfin, Caddy, WireGuard, and OpenVPN, with more to come.

I'm realizing row 2 is getting too long, so I need to redistribute these logos more evenly. I'll move some of the operating systems into row 1 to balance things out to roughly 16 items per row, keeping the infrastructure and platform tools together while spreading the OS options across both rows. I'm settling on keeping both MySQL and MariaDB since they're both legitimate technologies, and the total of 38 items works fine for the animation. Now I'm drafting the copy for this section with an eyebrow, title, and description that emphasizes how the product integrates with existing infrastructure and tools.

I'm adding a small disclaimer footnote beneath the marquee to clarify that the logos are shown for identification purposes only and don't imply any partnership or endorsement. For placement, I'll insert this marquee section right after the stats strip and before the value pillars section to maintain good visual rhythm. The base tone right after the hero works fine since they're visually distinct, and the panel band below provides good separation.
